device.category: 12-voice analogue polyphonic synthesizer, desktop, digitally controlled
device.based_on: Original design. The voice architecture (two oscillators, 4-pole VCF, common HPF) is in the Roland Juno tradition, but the manual makes no such claim.

sources.title: DeepMind 12D User Manual
sources.note: Full manual: 28 chapters. Used here: Controls (3), Signal Path (6), Programming (8), Block Diagram (13), Specifications (15), MIDI and NRPN tables (16, 17). Not used: Effects Reference (9), Menu System (7), Poly Chord appendix, SysEx (19).

architecture.signal_path_note: fully analogue voice under digital control; the DSP effects on the master bus can be hard-bypassed for an all-analogue path
architecture.polyphony_mode: 12-voice polyphonic with unison, mono and reduced-polyphony modes; poly chain across units
architecture.summary: Twelve identical analogue voices. Each has OSC1 (sawtooth and pulse, both switchable on, with pulse width modulation), OSC2 (square with tone modulation, independent pitch and level, syncable to OSC1), a white noise source, a 4-pole low-pass VCF switchable to 2-pole with resonance, envelope, LFO and keyboard tracking inputs, and a VCA. The voices sum into a common 6 dB/octave high-pass filter with a +12 dB bass boost, then an optional four-slot DSP effects engine, then volume and the stereo outputs. Every parameter is a digital value (mostly 0 to 255) controlling analogue circuitry, so every setting is stored in one of 1024 program memories and reachable over MIDI CC or NRPN. Modulation comes from two per-voice LFOs, three per-voice ADSR envelopes (VCA, VCF, MOD) with per-stage curves and looping or LFO triggering, and an 8-slot modulation matrix with 24 sources and about 130 destinations. Voice allocation offers poly, unison of 2 to 12 voices, mono with stacked voices, and limited polyphony, with selectable note priority, envelope trigger mode and vintage-style drift. An arpeggiator, a 32-step control sequencer, and chord and poly-chord memories sit on a master BPM clock.

modules.name: MIDI input
modules.description: All notes arrive over MIDI (DIN, USB or Wi-Fi). Produces note number, velocity, release velocity, channel aftertouch, pitch bend, mod wheel and the pedal and controller values that feed the modulation matrix. There is no keyboard on the 12D.

modules.name: Voice allocation
modules.description: Decides how the twelve voices are handed out to incoming notes: one per note, several per note in unison, one shared voice in mono, or a reduced pool. Sets note priority when voices run out, the envelope trigger rule for overlapping notes, and the drift generators that imitate vintage instability. Also holds pitch bend range, transpose and poly chain settings. Each voice gets its own independent drift.

modules.name: Portamento
modules.description: Glides pitch between notes. Time 0 to 10 s, with fourteen modes covering fingered (legato-only), fixed-rate, exponential and fixed-interval variants, and a balance control that lets one oscillator glide while the other jumps.

modules.name: OSC 1
modules.description: Dual-waveform analogue oscillator: sawtooth and pulse, each switchable on or off independently, so both can sound together. Pulse width from 50% (square) to 99%, modulated by a selectable source. Pitch modulation depth up to 36 semitones from a selectable source, with aftertouch and mod wheel depths on top. Three ranges.

modules.name: OSC 2
modules.description: Single-waveform analogue oscillator producing a square wave, with TONE MOD, which interrupts the pulse to change its harmonic content, from a selectable source. Independent pitch offset of plus or minus 12 semitones, its own level, optional hard sync to OSC1, and optional phase reset on key-down.

modules.name: Noise
modules.description: White noise source mixed with the oscillators. Per voice by inference: the level is a program parameter that the parameter drift acts on, and the manual describes the noise generator alongside the oscillators.

modules.name: Voice mixer
modules.description: Sums OSC1, OSC2 and noise before the filter. OSC1 has no level control of its own; balance is set with OSC2 LEVEL and NOISE LEVEL against a fixed OSC1.

modules.name: VCF
modules.description: Voltage-controlled low-pass filter, 4-pole by default and switchable to 2-pole. Resonance, envelope depth with polarity invert, LFO depth from a selectable LFO, keyboard tracking, velocity sensitivity and pitch bend to cutoff. A bass boost is also listed in its edit menu.

modules.name: VCA
modules.description: Per-voice amplifier, driven by the VCA envelope with adjustable depth and velocity sensitivity. Level from -12 dB to +6 dB. PAN SPREAD places each voice at a different position in the stereo field. A VCA-MODE switch chooses between a hotter and a cleaner characteristic.

modules.name: HPF
modules.description: 6 dB/octave high-pass filter common to all voices, applied after the voices sum. 20 Hz to 2 kHz. Also carries the BOOST switch, a +12 dB bass boost on the signal path.

modules.name: VCA envelope
modules.description: ADSR envelope that controls the VCA. Each stage has a time or level and a separately adjustable curve. Trigger mode selects key, LFO1, LFO2, loop or control sequencer; in the looping modes the sustain stage is skipped.

modules.name: VCF envelope
modules.description: ADSR envelope that controls filter cutoff. Each stage has a time or level and a separately adjustable curve. Trigger mode selects key, LFO1, LFO2, loop or control sequencer; in the looping modes the sustain stage is skipped.

modules.name: MOD envelope
modules.description: ADSR envelope that is a general-purpose modulation source for the matrix and the oscillators. Each stage has a time or level and a separately adjustable curve. Trigger mode selects key, LFO1, LFO2, loop or control sequencer; in the looping modes the sustain stage is skipped.

modules.name: LFO 1
modules.description: Low-frequency oscillator with seven shapes, rate from 0.041 Hz into the audio range at 65.4 Hz (1280 Hz when driven from the matrix), a delay with fade-in, key sync, sync to the master BPM with a clock divider, a slew control and a PHASE setting: POLY gives every voice its own free LFO, MONO shares one, SPREAD offsets each voice's LFO by a chosen number of degrees.

modules.name: LFO 2
modules.description: Low-frequency oscillator with seven shapes, rate from 0.041 Hz into the audio range at 65.4 Hz (1280 Hz when driven from the matrix), a delay with fade-in, key sync, sync to the master BPM with a clock divider, a slew control and a PHASE setting: POLY gives every voice its own free LFO, MONO shares one, SPREAD offsets each voice's LFO by a chosen number of degrees.

modules.name: Mod matrix
modules.description: Eight slots, each with a source, a destination and a bipolar depth. Sources include performance controllers, the LFOs and envelopes in several polarities, note number and velocity, the control sequencer and the voice number. Destinations are parameters rather than signal nodes, from oscillator pitch through every envelope stage and curve to effects levels. Some destinations are common to all voices. The table is stored with the program.

modules.name: Arpeggiator
modules.description: Arpeggiates held notes over 1 to 6 octaves in eleven orders, at the master BPM with a clock divider, gate time, swing and hold. CHORD maps one recorded chord across the keyboard from a single key; POLY CHORD maps different chords to individual keys.

modules.name: Control sequencer
modules.description: A 32-step sequencer of values rather than notes. Its output is a modulation source in the matrix and can also trigger the envelopes. Clock divider, length, swing, key sync and loop, and slew between steps.

modules.name: Effects engine
modules.description: Four-slot DSP effects engine (35 algorithms, ten routing modes) on the master bus, with a true analogue bypass. Deliberately not modelled in this iteration: it is treated as a pass-through so the analogue path stays complete. Its parameters do appear in the CC map and as matrix destinations.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Master volume, balanced stereo outputs and a headphone output that follows the main output.

mod_matrix.note: Destinations are listed as families rather than all 130 entries; ids here are positions in this list, not the instrument's NRPN destination numbers, which run 0 to 129 in the order of manual section 8.9.2. Effects destinations are listed but not modelled. The manual gives 22, 24 and 23 (NRPN 0 to 22) as the source count and 130, 132 and 130 (NRPN 0 to 129) as the destination count.

behaviours.name: Twelve voices, per-voice and common blocks
behaviours.rule: Every module marked per_voice exists twelve times, once per voice, with identical settings from the program and independent state (envelope position, LFO phase, drift). The voices sum after the VCA and everything from the HPF onward is single: one HPF, one bass boost, one effects engine, one volume.

behaviours.name: Digital control of an analogue voice
behaviours.rule: Every parameter is a stored digital value, mostly 0 to 255, driving analogue circuitry. A fader move updates the value; the display shows fader position, current value and stored value side by side. Everything is stored per program in 8 banks of 128, and reachable over CC (the panel faders) or NRPN (everything, at 8-bit resolution).

behaviours.name: Voice allocation modes
behaviours.rule: Poly: one voice per note, twelve notes. Unison-N: N voices per note, spread by UNISON DETUNE; 12/N notes. Mono-N: N stacked voices, one note. Poly-6 and Poly-8: one voice per note, pool limited. When an even number of voices are stacked they are spread symmetrically around the root and the root itself is not sounded; with an odd number one voice sits on the root.

behaviours.name: Note priority and voice stealing
behaviours.rule: When notes exceed voices, PRIORITY decides: Lowest steals the highest-sounding voice for a lower note, Highest the reverse, Last steals the least recently played. Not available in poly chain because excess notes go to the next unit instead.

behaviours.name: Envelope triggering on overlapping notes
behaviours.rule: ENV-TRIGGER sets what a new note does to an already-running envelope: Mono starts the attack from the current level, Retrigger resets to zero, Legato does not retrigger until all notes are released, One-shot resets and skips sustain, jumping from decay straight to release.

behaviours.name: Envelope shapes and curves
behaviours.rule: Each of attack, decay, sustain and release has a time or level and a separate curve value; the same four faders set either, switched by CURVES. Sustain's curve is a slope, letting the sustain stage rise or fall rather than hold. Times in seconds are not given for any stage.

behaviours.name: Envelopes as oscillators
behaviours.rule: Each envelope's trigger mode can be Key, LFO-1, LFO-2, Loop or Seq. In LFO modes the envelope fires on every LFO cycle; in Loop it refires at the end of its own release; in Seq on every control sequencer step. In all looping modes the sustain stage is skipped.

behaviours.name: Per-voice LFOs and phase
behaviours.rule: Each voice has its own two LFOs. PHASE selects POLY (independent and free), MONO (one LFO shared by all voices, so a chord wobbles together) or SPREAD (each voice offset by 1 to 254 degrees from the last, giving rotating or cascading modulation across a chord). LFO rate reaches 65.4 Hz from the fader and 1280 Hz from the matrix, so it can be used as an audio-rate modulator.

behaviours.name: LFO delay and fade
behaviours.rule: DELAY TIME is split 40/60: no output for the first 40% of the set time, then a fade-in over the remaining 60% to full depth. The fade envelope is itself a matrix source. The shape LED reflects the phase: off, half, full.

behaviours.name: OSC1 dual waveform and PWM
behaviours.rule: Sawtooth and pulse are independently switchable and sum when both are on. The PWM fader sets pulse width directly (50% square to 99% narrow) when PWM-SRC is Manual, or the modulation depth when a source is chosen. There is no separate manual width when a source is in use.

behaviours.name: OSC2 tone modulation
behaviours.rule: TONE MOD interrupts the OSC2 square wave within each half cycle, from none at 50% to an interrupt covering 60% of the half cycle at 100%. This is a form of pulse-width shaping with a different harmonic result from OSC1's PWM. Source selectable in the same way.

behaviours.name: Oscillator sync
behaviours.rule: SYNC forces OSC2 to restart on each OSC1 cycle. The manual shows three cases: OSC2 below OSC1, above, and below half, each producing a different sync timbre as OSC2 PITCH is swept.

behaviours.name: Filter modulation sum
behaviours.rule: Effective cutoff = FREQ + VCF envelope x ENV (inverted by INVERT) + selected LFO x LFO (plus aftertouch and mod wheel depths) + keyboard x KYBD + velocity x VELOCITY-SENS + pitch bend x P.BEND-FREQ + any matrix routes to VCF Freq. Summation law not stated; exponential domain assumed.

behaviours.name: Drift
behaviours.rule: OSC-DRIFT applies slow random pitch modulation to both oscillators; PARAM-DRIFT does the same to ten named modulation and filter parameters. Each voice has independent random generators for both, at a rate set by DRIFT-RATE from 25 to 50 ms at 0 to 2.5 to 5 s at 255, so voices drift apart rather than together.

behaviours.name: Master BPM
behaviours.rule: One clock, 20 to 275 BPM, from the RATE fader, TAP, or external MIDI clock on the interface chosen by CLOCK. The arpeggiator, the control sequencer and any LFO with ARP SYNC on divide it with their own clock dividers. When an LFO is synced its RATE fader picks a division instead of a frequency.

behaviours.name: Control sequencer
behaviours.rule: Thirty-two step values, not notes. The output is a matrix source, and can trigger envelopes. Length, clock divider, swing, key sync and looping, and a slew between steps. Turned on only from its edit page.

behaviours.name: Effects engine
behaviours.rule: Out of scope for this iteration. Four slots, 35 algorithms, ten routing modes, 24-bit 48 kHz, true analogue bypass. Its parameters occupy CC 62 to 114 and the last matrix destinations. Treated as unity pass-through here.

behaviours.name: Program memory
behaviours.rule: 1024 programs in 8 banks of 128, selected by bank select LSB 0 to 7 plus program change. COMPARE shows the difference between panel and stored values; WRITE saves with a name and category.

source_inconsistencies: The LFO RATE range at value 0 is given as 0.041 Hz (24.1 s) in 8.2.1 and 0.05371 Hz in 8.2.4.
CC 44 is printed as VCA Envelope Sustain and CC 56 as VCA Envelope Sustain Curve; both are in the VCF block and duplicate CC 40 and 52. Read as VCF.
NRPN 61 and 70 and 79 are each printed as an Attack Curve, duplicating 58, 67 and 76; by position they are the Release Curves.
LFO 1 Mono Mode is NRPN range 0 to 1 while LFO 2 Mono Mode is 0 to 255, although the notes column gives both the same Poly / Mono / Spread 1 to 254 encoding.
The number of matrix sources is given as 22 (signal path chapter), 24 (specifications) and 23 (NRPN 0 to 22); the printed list has 24.
The number of matrix destinations is given as 130 (signal path chapter and NRPN 0 to 129) and 132 (specifications and 8.9).

Section 3.1's numbered control list assigns descriptions to the wrong numbers in several places (OSC and VCA controls appear under item 10, 11 and 12 interchangeably); the manual_ref values here follow the section headings.
OSC2's KEY-DN-RESET is described in the OSC2 edit menu but its NRPN is named OSC Key Down Reset, implying both oscillators.
BOOST is a panel switch in the HPF block and a BASS-BOOST option in the VCF edit menu, and its NRPN is named VCF Bass Boost.

modelling_gaps.detail: The largest gap. Every envelope stage is 0 to 255 and no time in seconds is given at any value, for any of the three envelopes. Curves are likewise 0 to 255 with only qualitative pictures. A web search on 21 September 2026 found nothing published either: Behringer's product pages and reviews repeat the manual; a Gearspace summary of the 2016 Amazona preview quotes the designers as claiming attack times in the hundreds of microseconds rather than the usual 5 ms, and the open-source deepmind-midi project states explicitly that every time and frequency on the instrument is a byte whose curve has not been measured. The only route left is measurement of a unit.

Physical end points are given for oscillator pitch mod, PWM, OSC2 pitch and level, noise, VCF and HPF frequency, LFO rate and delay, drift rate and portamento; the mapping from 0 to 255 to those end points is not.
No resonance law, no self-oscillation statement, no account of the 2-pole response beyond the slope. The VCF is the sound of the instrument and the manual describes only its controls.
BALLSY versus TRANSPARENT is named and not explained.
Fixed and unspecified, so the mixer balance cannot be computed in absolute terms.
Twelve analogue voices will not be identical. The drift parameters model deliberate variation; inherent unit-to-unit and voice-to-voice tolerance is not documented and would need measurement.
Recorded as families with the instrument's numbering explained rather than as all 130 rows. Expanding to the full list is mechanical from section 8.9.2 when needed.
Excluded by design. The hooks are in place: fx module, CC ranges, matrix destinations.
Clock divider tables and the swing law are in appendix 1, not transcribed here.
Six extra depth controls (aftertouch and mod wheel into each oscillator's pitch mod and into the VCF LFO) are recorded as parameters but their interaction with the main depth is not stated.
